# Native DrawingML pattern-fill controls

Original XML generated by `tools/pattern_fill_fixture.py`, using python-docx
(MIT), lxml (BSD) and the repository's original drawing helpers. No corpus
document, font binary or third-party rendering implementation is redistributed.
The reference application exported `controls-native.pdf` from the exact
read-only source. The generator sets compatibility mode 15.

The 74 pages cover all 54 `ST_PresetPatternVal` values, omitted preset/colors,
group scaling, shape/group rotation, reflection, independent foreground and
background opacity, shifted origin, uneven frame dimensions, nonuniform group
scaling, ellipse clipping, inherited group fill, and monochrome/reversed-color
controls for three blended diagonal presets. Source XML passes eight schema
checks, including the supported published drawing extensions.

`tools/pattern_fill_reference.py` pins source/PDF hashes and records each native
tile's palette, eight rows of palette indices, PDF tile matrix, clipping bounds
and rendered page RGB hash at 144dpi. It verifies that every 16x16 PDF texture
consists of duplicated 2x2 cells. `sample96` contains RGB bytes encoded as hex
for the 8x8 interior sample at (232,192) in a 96dpi page raster.

Observed behavior:

- The reference application emits a 6pt square tile (16 samples at 0.375pt), equivalent to eight
  logical cells per axis. Scaling, rotation and reflection do not transform the
  tile's physical axes. The transformed shape still clips the fill.
- Omitted `prst` matches `pct5`. Omitted foreground/background resolve to
  black/white respectively.
- Shifted-origin and uneven-frame controls preserve the physical tile grid.
  PDF tile translations in the direct-fill controls fall on a 6pt grid. The
  inherited-group control emits a different, large translation; its phase needs
  separate verification before treating all fills as globally anchored.
- `dnDiag`, `upDiag` and `diagCross` have three palette colors, including
  intermediate blends. Monochrome and reversed-color controls preserve the
  evidence without guessing a blend/rounding formula.
- The translucent control's raw image samples appear premultiplied, but its
  composited native page sample agrees with standard independent paint opacity
  within two channel values. The painter uses ordinary premultiplied mixing,
  without an extra opacity correction based on raw PDF image bytes.
- The reference application emits a tiny off-diagonal tile coefficient (0.000000045) for the two
  rotated controls. PDFium changes the sampled tile period even though the
  coefficient's geometric effect is far below one pixel. The extractor retains
  raw samples and separately records `axisAlignedSample96`, obtained from an
  in-memory diagnostic copy with only coefficients below 1e-7 zeroed. Those
  samples match the painter exactly. The original PDF and its hash remain intact.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses: §20.1.8.47 (`pattFill`), §20.1.10.51
(`ST_PresetPatternVal`), §20.1.8.10 (`bgClr`) and §20.1.8.27 (`fgClr`). The
preset section supplies illustrations and points to .NET's HatchStyle names;
it does not provide the complete native pixel/phase conversion algorithm.
No numerical compatibility behavior above is claimed as a spec divergence
without a contradictory normative requirement.

The renderer now supports these presets, optional colors/preset, theme colors,
opacity, group inheritance, shape clipping and physical tile placement. Native
monochrome measurements define the blended-cell coverage; colored samples
agree within two channel values. Runtime data contains only logical cell
coverage, with arbitrary foreground/background colors resolved at import.

The browser regression compares 73 interior samples (including the two
explicitly normalized rotation diagnostics), checks ellipse clipping and
exercises editing/export/reopen/undo. The inherited group's native phase still
differs and is recorded without a passing-fidelity assertion. Patterned outlines
and picture backing fills remain unsupported. Source 114 is now editable with
its border artwork visible, but remains partial pending full fidelity review.
